run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The failing component is the cart workload in namespace astronomy-shop: its pod cart-74587775fc-n75bj is in a container crash loop (restart count 1 at 10:33:18, 3 at 10:34:19, 5 at 10:36:34; every termination reason 'Error', exitCode 139) and its own container log at 10:33:11 shows 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' thrown from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected (ValkeyCartStore.cs:101) / Initialize (line 71) / Program.Main (line 45). Because the cart container never finishes starting, the cart Service has no ready endpoint (only notReadyAddresses 10.244.7.228), so callers get connection refused on the cart ClusterIP 10.96.201.244:8080. This is visible as impact in the callers' own telemetry: frontend POST/GET /api/cart and its client spans oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and /AddItem return HTTP 500 / gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE with 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.201.244:8080 (2026-11-24T10:33:07.332Z)' at 10:33:09-10:33:11; checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder returns gRPC 13 INTERNAL 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout: ... connection refused' at 10:33:03-10:33:04 with its child CartService/GetCart span at code 14; load-generator user_view_cart / user_add_to_cart spans are HTTP 500. The dependency was investigated: valkey-cart-859985f49d-lxm5h is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, one process and five threads, logged 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 10:32:12 with no error lines through 10:33:15, its Service endpoint 10.244.234.174:6379 is ready, its Deployment has no command/args/env override, and the in-cluster OTel collector started a redis receiver against that pod at 10:32:48 without logged redis scrape failures in the window. No NetworkPolicy exists in the namespace and no duplicate pod IPs were found. A previous cart pod, cart-74587775fc-lw655, had in fact connected successfully to Redis ('Successfully connected to Redis' 10:32:17) and served AddItem/GetCart/EmptyCart until it was stopped at 10:32:54, when the same ReplicaSet created n75bj. So the diagnosis is partial: the cart workload's crash loop and its consequence on frontend/checkout are established, but why the replacement cart container cannot establish its Redis connection while valkey-cart is up is not established by the evidence available in this window (the inner exception was not captured and logs after 10:33:15 are outside the authorized window). Whole-stack startup at 10:32:08 explains the 10:32:49-10:33:09 pending alerts (ServiceEndpointDown for frontend/recommendation/email/product-catalog, DeploymentNotReady/PodStatusError/KubePodNotReady for accounting/checkout/fraud-detection/grafana/opensearch-0) and is not evidence of impact from this fault; product-catalog and payment showed only successful spans in the sampled traces.

The cart container's own log records at 2026-11-24T10:33:11 a fatal startup failure: 'Unhandled exception. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.201.244:8080 (2026-11-24T10:33:07.332Z)'; load-generator spans user_view_cart / user_add_to_cart also ended in HTTP 500.

checkout is affected by cart's unavailability: two oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans at 10:33:03/10:33:04 have status ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and otel.status_description 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 10.96.201.244:8080: connect: connection refused"', with child oteldemo.CartService/GetCart spans at rpc.grpc.status_code 14.

Dependency valkey-cart was checked and shows no failure of its own: pod valkey-cart-859985f49d-lxm5h is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, podIP 10.244.234.174, 1 process and 5 threads; its log shows 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 10:32:12.840 and no error lines between 10:30:00 and 10:33:15; its Service endpoint 10.244.234.174:6379 is a ready address.

The cart image/config is not the difference between the working and failing pod: the previous pod cart-74587775fc-lw655 (same ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc, created 10:32:08, node sregym-worker2) logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 10:32:17.902 and served AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync/EmptyCartAsync until its graceful shutdown at 10:32:54; the ReplicaSet created replacement pod cart-74587775fc-n75bj at 10:32:54, and that pod has never become ready.

Infrastructure-side causes checked at query time: there are no NetworkPolicy objects in namespace astronomy-shop, there are no duplicate pod IPs across the cluster, valkey-cart Deployment runs the plain valkey/valkey:9.0.1-alpine3.23 image with no command/args/env override and a 64Mi memory limit, and cart container memory working set was 2,220,032 bytes against a 160Mi limit (valkey-cart 2,027,520 bytes against 64Mi), so the cart crash is not accompanied by memory-limit pressure and last termination reason is 'Error' rather than OOMKilled.

The cart pod's network path is at least partly functional after 10:32:54: Calico received WorkloadEndpointUpdate messages for workload astronomy-shop/cart-74587775fc-n75bj (eth0, 10.244.7.228/32) at 10:32:54, 10:32:55, 10:32:56, 10:33:11 and 10:33:12, the pod's init container wait-for-valkey-cart logged 'valkey-cart (10.96.30.185:6379) open' at 10:32:55.508, and the pod had received 40,634 bytes on eth0 by 10:33:15.

Pending alerts evaluated at 10:32:49-10:33:09 are consistent with the simultaneous creation of the whole stack rather than with this cart fault: 23 'Scaled up replica set ... from 0 to 1' Deployment events occurred at 10:32:08, while the alert rules flagged ServiceEndpointDown for frontend/recommendation/email/product-catalog instances and DeploymentNotReady / PodStatusError / KubePodNotReady for accounting-5897477844-z5tkz, checkout-6c769b88b5-6xkzm, fraud-detection-7c945fdfbb-wb7wp, grafana-7b9cbf56f5-nb62x and opensearch-0, all of which show running, ready containers in the pod listing at 10:33:18.

In the sampled traces no error spans were returned for product-catalog or payment services, and the same frontend traces that failed on cart contain successful calls oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 (one followed by a product-catalog 'postgresql' span) at 10:33:10, so those dependency paths were working in those sampled traces.

Cart's startup Redis connection fails on the pod's name-resolution/TCP path to valkey-cart:6379 (rather than on a valkey outage): the cart pod's init container reached the same ClusterIP at 10:32:55.508 and valkey-cart itself is ready and serving, yet the cart container's own connect attempt throws and aborts. The mechanism (DNS resolution vs connection refused/timeout) cannot be read from the captured log, which contains only 'Wasn't able to connect to redis'.

valkey-cart being down, restarted, out of memory or resource-starved was considered as the cause of cart's Redis failure and is not supported: the pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, one process and five threads, logged 'Ready to accept connections tcp', has a ready endpoint at 10.244.234.174:6379 and no error lines in the window, and its Deployment has no command/args/env change and 2.03MB working set against a 64Mi limit.

A misconfigured cart image/template or a network-policy isolation was considered and is not supported: the failing pod and the earlier working pod share ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc and identical template env (VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, dnsPolicy ClusterFirst), and there are no NetworkPolicy objects in the namespace and no duplicate pod IPs in the cluster.

Capture the current cart container's newest log instance (crashes at 10:33:43, 10:35:00 and 10:36:24 are outside the authorized window) to read the inner exception of 'Wasn't able to connect to redis'; it will distinguish DNS resolution failure from TCP refusal/timeout and therefore the object to fix.

From inside pod cart-74587775fc-n75bj test resolution and reachability of valkey-cart (getent hosts valkey-cart / connect to 10.96.30.185:6379 and 10.244.234.174:6379) so the cart-to-Redis path can be classified as DNS, kube-proxy or pod-network, and compare with the same test from another pod on node sregym-worker2.

Add readiness/liveness probes to the cart container so a container that starts but cannot reach Redis is kept out of the Service endpoints, and verify whether the deletion of the previous cart pod at 10:32:54 was an intentional action, since its trigger is not visible in the retained events.

gaps: Why the replacement cart container cannot establish its Redis connection while valkey-cart is Ready and serving is unresolved: the captured log contains only 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' without the inner exception, and the container instances that crashed at 10:33:43, 10:35:00 and 10:36:24 wrote logs after the authorized window end (10:33:15), which neither the log tool nor Loki returned.

DNS-level evidence for the cart pod is missing: no CoreDNS/kube-dns log lines mentioning pod IP 10.244.7.228 or hostname valkey-cart were returned, so name-resolution failure versus TCP refusal/timeout cannot be distinguished.

The trigger for the removal of the previous cart pod cart-74587775fc-lw655 at 10:32:54 (kubelet 'Stopping container cart', graceful 'Application is shutting down', replacement pod created by the same ReplicaSet, no ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete event) is unknown; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

The Redis/Valkey integration could not authenticate (REDIS_AUTH_FAILED), so served clients, keyspace, latency and error statistics of valkey-cart could not be read directly; the redis-based tool view contributed no evidence.

No baseline exists for this environment: Jaeger traces start at 10:32:48 and the traces_span_metrics_calls_total series carry a single sample at 10:33:15 after all deployments were scaled from 0 to 1 at 10:32:08, so no pre-incident error-rate or latency comparison is possible and the 'cart' service error-status series (STATUS_CODE_ERROR) returned nothing in the whole window.

Scope of impact beyond the sampled traces is unknown: only sampled frontend, checkout, cart-owner and load-generator traces were inspected; other cart callers or unsampled requests are not covered, and the cart service itself emitted no spans after 10:32:53 because its container never started successfully.
No chaos/injection object (e.g. a chaos CRD namespace) is visible or queryable, so no object can be named as the applier of the cart pod deletion or of the cart-to-valkey connectivity failure.
next_steps: Read the newest cart container log instances (after 10:33:15) for the full inner exception of 'Wasn't able to connect to redis'.
Run a connectivity/DNS test to valkey-cart from the cart pod and from a sibling pod on node sregym-worker2 to locate the break (DNS, kube-proxy/ClusterIP, pod network).
Check whether a fault-injection/chaos experiment or an operator action targeted the cart workload at 10:32:54, since that deletion has no visible owner event.
After cart is restored, confirm recovery by cart readiness/endpoints and by absence of gRPC 14/HTTP 500 on /api/cart and PlaceOrder.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: The tool limited the query to the window 2026-11-24T10:32:30Z to 2026-11-24T10:33:15Z; this filter cannot be turned off.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
